html:
In August 1511 a Portuguese fleet under Afonso de Albuquerque captured Malacca, the richest port of Southeast Asia and the capital of the Malacca Sultanate.

Malacca controlled the Strait of Malacca, the narrow sea lane through which nearly all trade between India and China passed, and it was the market for the spices of the eastern islands. Portugal had just reached India by sea and taken Goa in 1510; see Portuguese seize Goa. Albuquerque's plan was to hold a few key ports, Goa, Malacca and Hormuz, and so command the trade of the Indian Ocean.

After weeks of fighting, the city fell. Albuquerque built the fortress later called A Famosa from the stones of mosques and royal tombs. Sultan Mahmud Shah fled and his heirs founded the Johor Sultanate. But Muslim traders moved to other ports such as Aceh and Brunei, and Malacca never regained its old role. The Dutch East India Company took it from Portugal in 1641.
sum: In August 1511 a Portuguese fleet under Afonso de Albuquerque captured Malacca, the richest port of Southeast Asia and the capital of the Malacca Sultanate.
